clue.text: Promise angry senator he is to be rehabilitated

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: rehabilitated means restored or remade, so the letters of senator and he are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A furious politician is to be reformed, and swears to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rehabilitated' rearranges SENATORHE into ONESHEART; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross one's heart is the gesture made when solemnly vowing that something is true.

clue.text: Supervised the positioning of a guard in the timber mill

definitions.text: the positioning of a guard in the timber mill

explanation.surface: Someone managed the fitting of a safety guard at a sawmill.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: in a timber mill a guard is placed over the saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Watched over and directed others' work is the past tense of oversee; and a blade guard sits above the cutting tool.

clue.text: Photo taken on the spur of the moment

definitions.text: taken on the spur of the moment

explanation.surface: A picture shot quickly without planning.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick photograph is a snapshot; and an impulsive, instant decision is called a snap judgement.

clue.text: Flier has a drink before bedtime

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a nightcap before going to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word; the second reading splits the answer as a night-time jar, JAR being British slang for a drink of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird; and a jar at night is a late tipple, jar being slang for a glass of beer.

clue.text: Lure French duke into a bishop's domain

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a see is the diocese a bishop governs
duc is the French word for duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat is enticed into a churchman's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice or tempt someone astray is a synonym of the verb lure.

clue.text: Single order given by her Majesty to a North European

indicators.note: order as a verb means arrange, so the letters of single are put in a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: The Queen gives one command to a northerner from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges SINGLE into ENGLIS; 'given by' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from England is a native of one of the countries of Europe.

clue.text: Summary reduction in numbers

explanation.surface: A brief report on cuts to staffing levels.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown is a quick précis of the main points; and running down a workforce means shrinking it.

clue.text: A vile tin not suited for air-conditioning

indicators.note: suited here means fitted or adapted, so the letters of a vile tin not are rearranged to suit

explanation.surface: A nasty tin can is no good for cooling a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like a negation of 'suited' but is part of the anagram fodder; 'suited' alone is the anagram indicator and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventilation supplies fresh air to a room, the basic job of any cooling or airflow system.

clue.text: Called into action, despite being crazy

indicators.note: into says the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a deed is an action
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Someone was summoned to act even though they were mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means mentally unbalanced or insane, a synonym of mad.

clue.text: Intelligence that is shown by a spirited servant

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or intelligence
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A clever lively servant shows sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirited' looks like 'lively' but means 'being a spirit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a spirit, a jinn, bound to serve whoever summons it from a lamp.

clue.text: Subject to a squeeze and up against it

explanation.surface: Someone squeezed and struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-pressed literally means pushed firmly; figuratively it means in difficulty, under heavy pressure.

clue.text: A section of the choral society performed as well

indicators.note: A section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the choir sang too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' looks like part of the definition but is a link: the definition is 'as well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means too or in addition, the same as the phrase as well.

clue.text: Persist in giving instruction to a billposter

explanation.surface: A poster-hanger told to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in giving' is a link; a billposter is told to glue up the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is the idiom; and a billposter's job is literally to paste the poster up.

clue.text: Embarked on a timber vessel

parts.note: a board is a plank of timber
a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone boarded a wooden boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Once passengers have embarked they are on the deck of the vessel, in nautical terms.

clue.text: Gloomy indication for the orchestra to strike up

definitions.text: indication for the orchestra to strike up

explanation.surface: A conductor's sombre signal to the players to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A downbeat mood is pessimistic; and in music the downbeat is the conductor's first beat of a bar.

clue.text: An antiseptic is otherwise no help

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of no help are set in another order

explanation.surface: A disinfectant is said to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, also called carbolic acid, was the first widely used surgical disinfectant.

clue.text: Milled grain is hard to display with style

parts.note: flour is grain ground in a mill
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Ground wheat is difficult to present elegantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish something is to wave or show it off ostentatiously.

clue.text: Ordinary people use a cheap paper label

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: The common folk read a tabloid with a price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag, as in ragtag and bobtail, means the rabble or riff-raff.

clue.text: Alluring appeal from American girl disheartened over love-affair

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second
disheartened means losing its heart, so the middle letter of gal goes

parts.note: gal is American slang for a girl
amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A dejected US girl gets charm out of a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is attractive, exciting charm, a synonym of alluring appeal.

clue.text: Vamoose as a result of a cuff about the ear

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a clout is a blow, a cuff
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flees after being boxed round the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a result of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leave quickly, the same as the phrasal verb to get out fast.

clue.text: Indulge in excessive perjury to be on top

parts.note: over as a prefix means too much, excessive
perjury is lying under oath, a lie

explanation.surface: A witness tells far too many falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indulge in' and 'to' are link words; 'perjury' leads the solver to courtroom lying, but the definition means to lie physically above.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlie is to lie upon or cover something beneath.

clue.text: Virginia and I enter a pub to no purpose

indicators.note: enter says the first pieces go inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Two people walk into a bar, achieving nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In vain means fruitlessly, without effect.

clue.text: Getting on one's feet means an enhanced reputation

parts.note: standing is status or reputation
up means raised or increased

explanation.surface: Rising from a chair improves one's status.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing up is rising to an upright position.

clue.text: His courage maybe won a woman's heart

definitions.text: His courage maybe won a woman's heart

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: heart means the central letter of the word won

explanation.surface: A brave man's valour wins over a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave man celebrated for courage is the classic champion who wins a lady's love.

clue.text: Salvationists try to make a pudding

parts.note: SA stands for the Salvation Army, whose members are Salvationists
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Salvation Army members attempt dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, cooked with milk as a British dessert.

clue.text: Hope returns around a hundred-or any great age

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps the other
returns means the word hope is read backwards

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Optimism comes back after a century or a long era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns HOPE into EPOH, which goes around C.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long historical period or era.

clue.text: Resourceful enough to store isinglass. How congenial!

indicators.note: to store means to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: able means capable, resourceful enough
isinglass is an old name for mica, the transparent mineral

explanation.surface: Someone clever enough to keep gelatine is a pleasant sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Isinglass is also a fish gelatine, but here it means the mineral used in stove windows. 'How' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and good-natured, a synonym of congenial.

clue.text: Very little results from an ebb tide

explanation.surface: Little comes of a receding tide.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: when the tide ebbs, the sea level falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny, insignificant amount is the idiom's meaning; and an ebbing tide literally lowers the sea.
